lessons.title: Noah and the Great Ark
lessons.keyLesson: God is faithful, and we should always trust and obey His Word.
lessons.memoryVerse: Noah did everything just as God commanded him.
lessons.intro: Long, long ago, the world had become a very unkind place. People fought, cheated and forgot about God. But one man still walked with God. His name was Noah. This is the story of how God kept one family safe — and gave the whole world a beautiful promise.
story: Noah loved God and listened to Him. One day, God spoke to Noah in a way he had never heard before. God told him that a great flood was coming to wash away all the wrong in the world. Then God gave Noah a very big job: build a huge boat, an ark, and bring his family inside.

The ark was enormous — longer than a football field! Noah and his sons cut wood, hammered nails and painted pitch inside and out. It took many, many years. Neighbours laughed at Noah. There was no rain, no river, not even a cloud in the sky. But Noah kept building, because Noah trusted God.

When the ark was finished, animals came from everywhere — two of every kind. Elephants and elephants, lions and lions, rabbits and rabbits. They walked right up the ramp two by two! Then Noah's family stepped inside, and God shut the door.

Rain fell for forty days and forty nights. Water covered the mountains. But inside the ark, Noah's family was safe, because God was with them. After the rain stopped, Noah sent out a dove. She came back with a fresh olive leaf in her beak — dry land was returning! When Noah's family finally stepped out, God placed a rainbow in the sky. It was a promise: never again would a flood destroy the whole earth.
points: God sees everything, and He cares about people who choose to do right.
Obeying God may not always be popular, but it is always worth it.
God keeps His promises — the rainbow still reminds us today.

questions.q: Why did God tell Noah to build the ark?
questions.a: Because a great flood was coming, and God wanted to keep Noah's family safe.

questions.q: How did Noah show that he trusted God?
questions.a: He obeyed God and built the ark, even when it had never rained and people laughed at him.

questions.q: What does the rainbow remind us of?
questions.a: God's promise that He will never again destroy the whole earth with a flood.

lessons.activity: Animal Pairs: Write or draw seven animals on small pieces of paper, making two cards for each animal. Mix them up and take turns finding the pairs — just like the animals came to the ark two by two. Then thank God for keeping His promises.
lessons.prayer: Dear God, thank You for the story of Noah. Help us to obey You even when it is hard, and to trust Your promises every day. Amen.

lessons.title: David and Goliath
lessons.keyLesson: With God on our side, no problem is bigger than His power.
lessons.intro: Goliath was a giant — taller than the tallest door, with armour that shone in the sun. Every morning and every evening he shouted at God's people, and everyone was afraid. Everyone, that is, except a young shepherd boy named David.
story: David was the youngest of eight brothers. While his brothers served in the army, David stayed home looking after his father's sheep. One day his father sent him to take food to his brothers. When David arrived at the camp, he heard Goliath shouting insults at God and at Israel's army.

The soldiers ran away. Even King Saul was afraid. But David said, Who is this giant that he should insult the living God? David remembered how God had helped him fight a lion and a bear while he guarded his sheep. He knew God would help him now.

Saul offered David his armour, but it was far too big. Instead, David chose five smooth stones from a stream and walked towards Goliath with his sling and his faith. Goliath laughed at him. David answered, You come against me with a sword and a spear, but I come against you in the name of the Lord Almighty.

David put a stone in his sling, swung it round and round, and let it fly. The stone hit Goliath right on the forehead, and the giant fell down! The whole army of Israel shouted with joy. David did not win because he was strong. He won because he trusted a great big God.
points: The size of your problem does not limit the size of your God.
Faith often starts with the small things — David learned to trust God while watching sheep.
Courage is not the absence of fear; it is doing the right thing with God's help.

questions.q: What did Goliath use to frighten God's people?
questions.a: His huge size, his loud voice, his sword, spear and armour.

questions.q: What did David take with him to fight Goliath?
questions.a: A sling and five smooth stones — and his trust in God.

questions.q: What can we learn from David's courage?
questions.a: That God is bigger than any problem, and we can face challenges when we trust Him.

lessons.activity: Stones of Courage: Find five smooth stones or make five paper stones. On each one, write a word that describes God — for example Strong, Faithful, Loving, Mighty, Near. Keep one in your pocket this week as a reminder that God is with you.
lessons.prayer: Dear God, thank You that You are bigger than every giant we face. Help us to be brave like David, and to remember that the battle belongs to You. Amen.

lessons.title: Daniel in the Lions' Den
lessons.keyLesson: Faithfulness in prayer gives us courage to keep honouring God.
lessons.memoryVerse: My God sent his angel, and he shut the mouths of the lions.
lessons.intro: Daniel loved God so much that he prayed three times a day, every day. When a new law made prayer against the law, Daniel had a choice: stop praying, or keep praying and trust God. His answer became one of the most famous stories of courage in the Bible.
story: Daniel was an old man now, and he had served God faithfully all his life. He was so wise and honest that the king planned to put him in charge of the whole kingdom. Some jealous officials did not like this at all, so they made a plan to get rid of him.

They convinced the king to make a new law: for thirty days, everyone must pray only to the king. Anyone who prayed to any other god or person would be thrown into a den of hungry lions. The officials knew Daniel would never stop praying to the one true God.

Daniel did exactly what he had always done. He opened his windows towards Jerusalem, knelt down and prayed three times a day, giving thanks to God. The officials rushed to tell the king, and the king was very sad — but the law could not be changed.

Daniel was thrown into the lions' den. The king stayed awake all night, worrying. Very early the next morning he hurried to the den and called out, Daniel, has your God saved you? Daniel answered, My God sent his angel, and he shut the mouths of the lions. They have not hurt me, because I was found innocent in his sight. Daniel was lifted out without a scratch, and the king praised the God who rescues.
points: Daniel did not wait for a crisis to pray — prayer was his daily habit.
We can honour God even when it is difficult or unpopular.
God is able to protect us, and He is always with us in the den.

questions.q: How many times a day did Daniel pray?
questions.a: Three times a day.

questions.q: What did the jealous officials want the king to do?
questions.a: Make a law that everyone must pray only to the king, so Daniel would be punished.

questions.q: How did God protect Daniel?
questions.a: He sent an angel to shut the mouths of the lions so they could not hurt Daniel.

lessons.activity: Prayer Windows: Make a paper window with two opening flaps. Inside, write or draw three things you want to pray about this week. Open the flaps each day and pray, just like Daniel prayed by his window three times a day.
lessons.prayer: Dear God, thank You for Daniel's example. Help us to make prayer a habit every day, and to trust You even when it is hard to do the right thing. Amen.

lessons.title: The Boy Jesus in the Temple
lessons.keyLesson: Jesus grew in wisdom and favour — and we can grow like Him.
lessons.memoryVerse: And Jesus grew in wisdom and stature, and in favor with God and man.
lessons.intro: The Bible tells us very little about Jesus when He was a boy. But one story gives us a wonderful window into those years — the time twelve-year-old Jesus stayed behind in the Temple, listening, asking questions and amazing the teachers.
story: Every year, Jesus' family travelled to Jerusalem for the Passover festival. When Jesus was twelve, they made the journey together with a large group of relatives and friends. After the festival, Mary and Joseph began the trip home, thinking Jesus was somewhere in the crowd.

But Jesus was not with them. When they could not find Him, they hurried back to Jerusalem. For three days they searched. Finally, they found Him in the Temple courts, sitting among the teachers, listening to them and asking them questions. Everyone who heard Him was amazed at His understanding and His answers.

Mary asked, Son, why have you treated us like this? We have been anxiously searching for you. Jesus answered, Didn't you know I had to be in my Father's house? Mary and Joseph did not fully understand, but Mary treasured these things in her heart.

Jesus went back home to Nazareth with His parents and was obedient to them. The Bible says He grew in wisdom and stature, and in favour with God and man. He learned, He asked questions, He helped His family — and He grew in every way.
points: Jesus was once a child, so He understands what growing up is like.
God wants us to grow in wisdom — asking questions is a wonderful way to learn.
Honouring our parents and learning from teachers pleases God.

questions.q: Where did Mary and Joseph find Jesus after three days?
questions.a: In the Temple courts in Jerusalem, sitting among the teachers, listening and asking questions.

questions.q: How did Jesus grow?
questions.a: In wisdom and stature, and in favour with God and man.

questions.q: What is one way we can grow like Jesus?
questions.a: By asking questions, learning from teachers and parents, and obeying God.

lessons.activity: Wonder Jar: Decorate a jar and fill it with paper slips. On each slip, write a question you have about God or the Bible. Pick one each day this week, look it up with a parent or teacher, and add what you learn to a notebook.
lessons.prayer: Dear Jesus, thank You for showing us what it looks like to grow in wisdom. Help us to love learning, ask good questions and obey those who care for us. Amen.

lessons.title: Jesus Calms the Storm
lessons.keyLesson: Even when life feels stormy, Jesus is with us and He is in control.
lessons.memoryVerse: Even the wind and the waves obey him!
lessons.intro: The Sea of Galilee could be calm one minute and wild the next. Jesus' friends were experienced fishermen, but one night a storm frightened them so much that they thought they were going to die. Then Jesus did something no one expected.
story: Jesus had been teaching crowds of people all day. He was tired, so He said to His disciples, Let us go over to the other side of the lake. They climbed into a boat, and Jesus fell asleep on a cushion at the back.

Soon a furious storm came up. Waves crashed over the boat, and water began to fill it. The disciples were terrified. They woke Jesus and said, Teacher, don't you care if we drown? Jesus stood up, said to the wind, Quiet! Be still! — and everything became completely calm.

The wind stopped. The waves lay flat. The disciples were amazed and a little afraid. They said to each other, Who is this? Even the wind and the waves obey him! They were beginning to understand that Jesus was not just a great teacher. He was the Son of God.

We all face storms — times when we feel afraid, sad or worried. Jesus may not always take the storm away immediately, but He promises to be with us in it. We can bring our fears to Him, because He cares.
points: Storms can come suddenly, but Jesus is always with us in the boat.
Jesus has power over nature — nothing is impossible for Him.
We can tell Jesus exactly how we feel, because He cares about us.

questions.q: What was Jesus doing when the storm began?
questions.a: He was asleep on a cushion at the back of the boat.

questions.q: What did Jesus say to the wind and the waves?
questions.a: Quiet! Be still! — and the storm stopped completely.

questions.q: What can we do when we feel afraid?
questions.a: We can talk to Jesus, remember that He is with us, and ask Him for peace.

lessons.activity: Calm Jar: Fill a clear jar with water, a spoon of glitter and a drop of food colouring. Shake it and watch the glitter swirl like a storm. As you wait for it to settle, say a short prayer and breathe slowly. Remember: Jesus can calm the storms inside us too.
lessons.prayer: Dear Jesus, thank You that You are with us in every storm. When we are afraid, help us to remember Your power and Your love. Speak peace to our hearts today. Amen.

lessons.title: The Good Samaritan
lessons.keyLesson: A neighbour is anyone who needs our kindness — and kindness costs something.
lessons.intro: One day, a man asked Jesus, Who is my neighbour? Jesus answered with a story about a robbery, a road, and three very different people. The surprise at the end of the story still challenges us today.
story: A Jewish man was travelling from Jerusalem to Jericho. The road was rocky and lonely, and robbers were known to hide there. Suddenly, they attacked him. They took his clothes, beat him and left him half dead on the side of the road.

After a while, a priest came walking down the road. When he saw the hurt man, he crossed over to the other side and kept walking. Later, a Levite — a temple helper — came by. He looked at the man, but he also passed by on the other side.

Then a Samaritan came along. Samaritans and Jews did not like each other at all. But when the Samaritan saw the hurt man, his heart filled with pity. He bandaged the man's wounds, poured on oil and wine, lifted him onto his own donkey and took him to an inn. The next day he paid the innkeeper and promised to pay for anything else the man needed.
Jesus asked, Which of these three do you think was a neighbour to the man who fell into the hands of robbers? The answer was clear: the one who had mercy on him. Jesus said, Go and do likewise.
points: Love is not just a feeling — it shows up in helpful actions.
Our neighbour is anyone who needs us, even someone who is different from us.
Kindness may cost time, effort or money, but it is always worth it.

questions.q: What happened to the man on the road to Jericho?
questions.a: Robbers attacked him, took his clothes and left him half dead.

questions.q: Who stopped to help the hurt man?
questions.a: A Samaritan — someone the man would not have expected to help him.

questions.q: What did Jesus tell us to do?
questions.a: Go and do likewise — show mercy and kindness to anyone who needs it.

lessons.activity: Kindness Challenge: Write seven acts of kindness on paper slips — one for each day of the week. Put them in a jar and pull one out each morning. Draw a small heart in your journal every time you complete one.
lessons.prayer: Dear God, thank You for loving us even when we were far from You. Help us to notice people who need help and to show kindness like the Good Samaritan. Amen.

lessons.title: The Lord's Prayer
lessons.keyLesson: Prayer is simply talking to our loving Father — and Jesus taught us how.
lessons.memoryVerse: Our Father in heaven, hallowed be your name.
lessons.intro: The disciples watched Jesus pray and realised there was something wonderful about the way He talked to God. So they asked Him, Lord, teach us to pray. Jesus gave them a prayer that Christians have prayed ever since.
story: Jesus first reminded His friends that prayer is not a performance. We do not pray to impress other people or to use lots of fancy words. We pray to our Father in heaven, who loves us and already knows what we need.

Then Jesus prayed: Our Father in heaven, hallowed be your name, your kingdom come, your will be done, on earth as it is in heaven. He began by honouring God. God is not a vending machine or a distant stranger — He is our Father, and His name is holy.

Jesus continued: Give us today our daily bread. And forgive us our debts, as we also have forgiven our debtors. And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one. We can ask God for what we need, say sorry for what we have done wrong, forgive others, and ask for His help to stay strong.
The Lord's Prayer is like a map for our prayers. We can pray it word for word, or we can use each line to guide our own words. Either way, we are talking to a Father who is listening.
points: Prayer is a conversation with our loving Father, not a performance.
We begin by honouring God and asking for His will, not just our own.
We can bring our needs, our mistakes, our forgiveness and our struggles to God.

questions.q: Why did the disciples ask Jesus to teach them to pray?
questions.a: They saw the way Jesus prayed and wanted to learn to pray like Him.

questions.q: How does the Lord's Prayer begin?
questions.a: Our Father in heaven, hallowed be your name.

questions.q: What are some things we can pray about?
questions.a: God's honour, His will, our daily needs, forgiveness, forgiving others, and help to stay away from temptation.

lessons.activity: Prayer Hand: Trace your hand on paper. On each finger write one part of prayer: Praise, Thanks, Sorry, Others, Me. Use your five fingers to guide your prayers each day this week.
lessons.prayer: Our Father in heaven, hallowed be your name. Thank You for teaching us to pray. Help us to talk with You every day and to trust Your good will for our lives. Amen.

lessons.title: The Lost Sheep
lessons.keyLesson: Every child is precious to God — He will never give up on us.
lessons.memoryVerse: Rejoice with me; I have found my lost sheep.
lessons.intro: Jesus told a story about a shepherd with one hundred sheep. When one little lamb wandered away, the shepherd did not shrug his shoulders. He left the ninety-nine and went looking until he found it.
story: Sheep are not very good at taking care of themselves. They wander, they get stuck, they get lost. That is why they need a shepherd. A good shepherd knows every sheep by name, and he watches over them day and night.

One day, the shepherd counted his sheep and found only ninety-nine. One was missing. He did not say, Oh well, ninety-nine is still a lot. He left the ninety-nine in the open country and went after the lost sheep until he found it.
When he found it, he did not scold it. He lifted it onto his shoulders, joyfully carried it home, and called his friends and neighbours: Rejoice with me; I have found my lost sheep!

Jesus explained that there is more rejoicing in heaven over one sinner who repents than over ninety-nine righteous people who do not need to repent. Every person matters to God — including you. When we wander away, God comes looking for us and welcomes us home with joy.
points: Every person is precious to God — no one is too small or too far away.
God does not give up on us, even when we wander away.
Heaven celebrates when someone comes back to God.

questions.q: How many sheep did the shepherd have?
questions.a: One hundred sheep.

questions.q: What did the shepherd do when one sheep was lost?
questions.a: He left the ninety-nine and searched until he found the lost sheep.

questions.q: What does this story teach us about God?
questions.a: That God loves each one of us, searches for us when we are lost, and celebrates when we come back to Him.

lessons.activity: Sheep Search: Hide ten cotton balls or paper sheep around a room. Ask a family member to find them all while you count. Talk about how God never stops looking for us — and how we can help others feel found and loved too.
lessons.prayer: Dear God, thank You that we are precious to You. Help us to stay close to You like sheep close to their shepherd, and to show love to people who feel lost. Amen.

lessons.title: Joseph and His Colourful Coat
lessons.keyLesson: God can turn even painful stories into something good.
lessons.memoryVerse: You intended to harm me, but God intended it for good.
lessons.intro: Joseph had big dreams and a father who loved him very much. His brothers were jealous, and their choices led Joseph into slavery and prison. But through every twist, God was quietly writing a bigger story.
story: Joseph was the favourite son of his father Jacob. Jacob gave him a beautiful coat of many colours. Joseph's brothers were jealous. To make things worse, Joseph told them about his dreams — dreams in which his brothers' sheaves of grain bowed down to his sheaf.

One day, Jacob sent Joseph to check on his brothers. When they saw him coming, they made a terrible plan. They threw him into an empty well, then sold him to traders on their way to Egypt. They dipped his coat in goat's blood and lied to their father, saying a wild animal had killed him.

In Egypt, Joseph worked as a slave in Potiphar's house. God was with Joseph, and everything he did succeeded. But then Potiphar's wife told a lie about him, and Joseph was sent to prison. Even there, God was with him. Joseph interpreted dreams for Pharaoh's cupbearer and baker, and eventually Pharaoh himself heard about it.

God gave Joseph the meaning of Pharaoh's troubling dream: seven years of plenty were coming, followed by seven years of famine. Pharaoh put Joseph in charge of storing food. When the famine came, people from everywhere came to Egypt to buy grain — including Joseph's brothers. They did not recognise him, but Joseph recognised them. Eventually he revealed who he was and forgave them. What they meant for evil, God used to save many lives.
points: Jealousy can lead people to do terrible things, but God can bring good out of bad.
God was with Joseph in the palace and in the prison — He never left him.
Forgiveness sets us free and allows God's bigger story to continue.

questions.q: Why were Joseph's brothers jealous of him?
questions.a: Because their father loved Joseph best and gave him a special colourful coat; Joseph also had dreams about his brothers bowing to him.

questions.q: Where did Joseph end up after his brothers sold him?
questions.a: In Egypt, where he worked as a slave in Potiphar's house and later was put in prison.

questions.q: How did God use Joseph's story for good?
questions.a: Joseph stored food before the famine and saved many lives — including his own family.

lessons.activity: Coat of Many Colours: Cut a simple coat shape from paper and decorate it with bright colours. Inside the coat, write one way God has helped your family through a difficult time. Hang it up as a reminder that God can write a good story.
lessons.prayer: Dear God, thank You that You are always working, even when we cannot see it. Help us to trust You in hard times, forgive people who hurt us, and remember that You can bring good out of any story. Amen.

lessons.title: The Helper Jesus Promised
lessons.keyLesson: The Holy Spirit is our Helper — He teaches, comforts and helps us live like Jesus.
lessons.memoryVerse: The Holy Spirit will teach you all things.
lessons.intro: Before Jesus went back to heaven, He knew His friends would feel sad and afraid. So He made them a wonderful promise: I will not leave you alone. The Father will send you a Helper — the Holy Spirit.
story: Jesus told His disciples that He was going away to prepare a place for them. They did not want Him to go. But Jesus said, If you love me, keep my commands. And I will ask the Father, and he will give you another advocate to help you and be with you forever — the Spirit of truth.

Jesus explained that the world cannot see or know the Holy Spirit, but His followers would know Him, because He lives with us and in us. The Holy Spirit is not a force or a feeling. He is God — a Person who teaches, reminds, comforts and guides.

Jesus said, The Holy Spirit will teach you all things and will remind you of everything I have said to you. He also gave them peace: Peace I leave with you; my peace I give you. Do not let your hearts be troubled and do not be afraid.

After Jesus returned to heaven, the Holy Spirit came at Pentecost. The disciples were filled with courage, wisdom and power to tell everyone about Jesus. The same Holy Spirit helps us today — to understand the Bible, to make good choices, to pray and to become more like Jesus.
points: The Holy Spirit is God, and He lives with everyone who trusts Jesus.
He teaches us, reminds us of Jesus' words and comforts us when we are afraid.
We can ask the Holy Spirit to help us every day — He is our Helper.

questions.q: What did Jesus promise to send to His disciples?
questions.a: The Holy Spirit — the Helper who would teach, remind and comfort them.

questions.q: What are some things the Holy Spirit does?
questions.a: He teaches us, reminds us of Jesus' words, comforts us, guides us and helps us live like Jesus.

questions.q: How can we welcome the Holy Spirit's help?
questions.a: By praying, reading the Bible, listening to God and asking Him to help us make good choices.

lessons.activity: Fruit of the Spirit Basket: Draw a basket and cut out nine paper fruits. On each fruit, write one fruit of the Spirit from Galatians 5:22–23 — love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness and self-control. Put one in the basket each time you show that fruit during the week.
lessons.prayer: Dear God, thank You for sending the Holy Spirit to be our Helper. Fill us with Your peace and help us to grow in love, joy, patience and kindness. Teach us to listen to You every day. Amen.
